decorative-vs-meaningful-text-exemption: Low-contrast text gets misjudged: purely ornamental words are flagged as failures, while faint-but-meaningful content like a price or status watermark is wrongly excused as decoration.
logotype-brand-exemption-and-erosion: Brand logos are exempt from contrast rules, but the exemption is abused when ordinary styled headings, taglines, or clickable logo-links with poor contrast hide behind it.
faux-disabled-vs-genuinely-inactive-ui: A button greyed out to look disabled but still clickable must meet contrast rules, yet checkers can't tell whether the control is truly inactive without operating it.
effective-background-across-cascade-and-: Figuring out the real colour behind text is hard when it comes from a parent element, an overlapping layer, or a see-through panel, so contrast tools guess wrong.
background-image-least-contrast-per-lett: Text over a photo can be readable on average but unreadable where a bright patch sits behind a few letters, which best-case contrast checks miss.
aa-thresholds-and-large-text-classificat: Using the wrong contrast threshold: normal text needs 4.5:1 and large text only 3:1, but deciding whether a given font counts as 'large' takes human judgement.
state-dependent-text-contrast: Text that only appears on hover, focus, typing, or errors (like placeholder or error messages) must also be readable, but tools only check the initial page.
picture-with-significant-other-content-e: Text inside a real photo (like a street sign) is exempt, but text drawn as an image just for a fancy look is not.
